claims.statement: The transcription pipeline is the deterministic media stage that runs ffmpeg audio extract, optional scenedetect slide extraction, and OpenRouter STT, and it does not call slides or summarize backends. Those paid/network stages live in the manifest-gated orchestrator that runs after the media stage.

The pipeline reuses pipeline._run_command as the sole child-process seam for external binaries, including the ffmpeg calls used both for audio extract and for explicit time-sliced chunking inside the transcribe stage, and each call is wrapped with a configurable timeout.

Chunking uses one explicit ffmpeg -ss/-t call per part with segment_seconds + overlap_seconds length, rather than -f segment, because the segment muxer has no overlap option and overlapping parts are required for cross-chunk speaker reconciliation.

The OpenRouter STT seam posts a JSON base64 body (raw base64, not a data URI) to /audio/transcriptions, uses verbose_json plus a per-model provider diarization toggle for microsoft/mai-transcribe-2 when diarize is true, retries 429/5xx with bounded backoff, fails immediately on 400, and never logs the API key, headers, or base64 audio.

The transcribe stage produces a flat transcript under diarize == false or when no labels are present, and a Speaker <ID>: <text> transcript with no timestamp markers when diarized labels exist, driven by render_transcript after stitch and reconcile_speakers map per-chunk provider labels onto a global speaker registry using the overlap window.

The transcribe stage is partially idempotent via a segments.json manifest under transcribe_work.<name>/ that records completed parts so they are never re-issued, and it discards and rechunks the work dir when stored segment_seconds/overlap_seconds differ from the current config (parameter guard E5).

process_recording processes one MP4 through audio extract, optional slides, and transcribe stages and returns a RecordingResult with new versus skipped artifacts, while process_all runs it over every MP4 in recordings_dir in sorted order.

_run_command is the sole child-process seam: it builds a duct expression with optional stdout redirection, polls to enforce the timeout, raises PipelineTimeoutError after killing the child on expiry, and lets non-zero exits surface as duct.StatusError.

Audio extract runs ffmpeg with audio-only flags under the ffmpeg timeout and is skipped when the MP3 exists with have_mp3 still gating transcription; slides extraction runs scenedetect under the scenedetect timeout only when slides are enabled and is skipped when the slide directory exists.

chunk_audio slices audio with explicit per-part ffmpeg -ss and -t calls carrying segment plus overlap length because the segment muxer cannot express overlap, computing part count as ceil(duration divided by segment_seconds) and falling back to a single part when duration is unknown.

Transcription duration comes from a best-effort ffprobe call through the pipeline _run_command seam with a fixed timeout and temp-file cleanup, returning None so chunking falls back to one part when probing fails or yields non-numeric output.

stitch offsets each chunk by index times segment_seconds onto a monotonic timeline, reconcile_speakers maps local labels to global ids via the overlap window with unmatched speakers getting a new id plus warning and later chunks skipping the leading overlap duplicates, and render_transcript emits Speaker ID lines without timestamps or flat concatenated raw text when undiarized.

transcribe_recording stores per-part progress in transcribe_work segments.json with immediate persistence and a segment_seconds and overlap_seconds parameter guard that discards stale work, skips done parts on resume, while the pipeline driver skips transcription entirely when the TXT artifact already exists.

The pipeline stays media-only with per-stage timeouts from config timeouts for ffmpeg, scenedetect, and transcribe stages and never invokes the paid slides-description or summarize backends, which run later in the manifest-gated orchestrator.
